steps.path: Setup wizard, the between-sessions screen, the tour, tips, Projects, Settings and the first warnings
steps.headline: This is what done means for the first-run guide.

rows.statement: The buddy stands in a corner of the real app with a speech bubble that points at the control each stop is about.
rows.note: but i think i do want to add a line to the system prompt or a new tool to better allow the assistant to view/explain it's own capabilities. "If a user asks you how to do x or y or about how youcoded works or its settings menus, use *youcoded-info-desk* to answer. this can be roadmapped for now.

rows.statement: The tour starts on its own once, right after setup; Show me around in Settings brings it back any time.
Every stop is a sentence or two and Next; a stop with an obvious action also offers a button that does it.
rows.note: should also open some settings pages and projects view so the user can see what the assistant is talking about as it explains.

rows.statement: The tour has eight stops in this order: buddy, sessions, projects, models and providers, tags and notes, files, make it yours, help.
The sentence about the assistant changing and deleting files lives on the setup wizard, where nobody can skip past it.
rows.note: that reminds me. as part of this work, i also want to add some clearer warnings/popups the first time some things are done. like when a user enables skip permissions or full auto, or uses a small small model for the first time (like 9b-40b class) we should very cleary explain that these actions are more likely to result in damage and data loss, especially when used with less capable models. we should be honest without being scary, so a user just has pragmatic expectations. full auto and skip permissions should require a "i understand" checkbox with a continue button. just want to cover our asses for obvious liability issues

rows.statement: The sign-in card carries the file-safety sentence in the wording Destin wrote, not any of the three offered.
rows.note: "With your permission, the assistant may create, change, or delete files on your device. Create backups for anything you cannot replace.

rows.statement: The file-safety wording on the sign-in card is the one from the slide before, word for word.
The wizard's last card says the tour is coming, instead of listing three things to try; the spinner line stays.
A tip is the same buddy and bubble in a corner of the main window, one at a time, with a Got it button.
Each tip fires at the moment it becomes relevant, not on a calendar; about eight in all, ending when they run out.
Never more than one tip per sitting, each shown once, and never while the assistant is answering.
Every tip carries Got it and Stop showing tips; Stop showing tips ends all of them for good.
These are the eight tips, each fired by its named moment: tags, notes, projects, resume, local models, buddy floater, themes, help.
With no projects yet, the Projects screen shows an explainer card, one Add a project button and the buddy beside it.
The word "artifacts" is gone from the empty Projects screen; once a project exists, the screen is today's again.
rows.note: this button should be the full width of the text. can improve the copy to be clear/concise for new users with no context. tagline "folder you keep coming back to" feels a bit like meaningless word salad.

rows.statement: A brand-new person sees "Start your first session", one sentence on what a session is, and the New Session form already open.
Resume is hidden while there is nothing to resume; once a session exists to resume, the screen is today's again.
rows.note: this is good. i'm also realizing we should probably create a mechanism for users to launch a new session without using a project folder at all. not sure how we'd do this. could be a zero-context/instruction launch, or we could start all users with a new "Home" directory or something that contains some overarching/global assistant settings? maybe just start with a none/zero-context option for now and add the other to roadmap?

rows.statement: A project's Conversations tab with none uses the standard empty state, and the session note's placeholder says what a note is for.
The community link on the tour's last stop and the help page goes to r/youcoded.
Settings has a Help & feedback page; Report a bug stays reachable from Development too.
A Help & feedback row sits above Development in the settings drawer; Development and everything below it are unchanged.
Help & feedback holds Show me around, the Tips for new users switch, Community on Reddit, Report a bug, Known issues and the version.
The tour and tips run only for someone who finishes setup after this ships; existing users see nothing pop up.
The tour and tips ship on desktop only; the empty screens and the Help page reach the phone and browser as well.
The first time Skip Permissions is switched on, an explainer with an I-understand checkbox appears; Turn it on stays greyed until ticked.
The first session on a small model gets a short, honest explainer with Got it and no checkbox, shown once only.
Picking Full auto the first time shows the same dialog shape with its own words, the always-asks list verbatim, and the checkbox.
The bubble's buttons read Back, Skip tour, Next; Next (or Done) is filled at the far right, Skip tour bare text.
"This takes about a minute" is gone; stop 1 greets you as your buddy and says where to find it again.
Stops 2 to 8 open New Session, Projects, Cloud providers, Appearance and Help & feedback for real, closing each as the tour moves on.
Stop 6 says your signed-in account answers you, and a different or free local AI service is added here; no "provider" or "model".
The empty Projects card reads "Projects keep your work together" with the approved three sentences, and Add a project is as wide as the text.
The wizard's last card says "Your assistant will show you around once the app opens."
The sign-in card's file-safety sentence is Destin's wording exactly, ending at "cannot replace."
The Project Folder list starts with a "No folder" entry; that session runs in an empty folder the app owns, with no instructions.
